perQuestion.answer: The project rejected frequent re-centering because 720-day backtests showed it lost to passive wide ranges even in flat regimes. The mechanism was that while narrowing earned ~4× more fees, the implied loss (IL) from re-centering realized the divergence, eroding ~$1.9k–$2.9k more than the fee gains. The team concluded that a narrow range acts like a short gamma position, where every posture change realizes a loss. The initial belief that IL was negligible in flat markets was proven false, and the strategy ultimately remained wide passive LP.

perQuestion.answer: The bot never opened, closed, or re-ranged positions automatically because it was designed to run in PROPOSE mode, where it only generates signals and ready transactions that require manual human signature. The documentation explicitly states that "the bot executes nothing on its own" and that "AUTO mode was never enabled." Full automatic execution was part of the original plan (Phase 4), but it was "Not built as planned." The system relied on a human owner to sign transactions in a browser wallet (Rabby) or approve actions via the cockpit UI, meaning automatic execution was technically possible in the architecture but never implemented or activated.

perQuestion.answer: The project's design notes explain that a browser cannot serve as the automation engine because "a closed laptop means a dead autopilot," so the bot must run as a separate 24/7 process. citations.quote: obie nogi crypto = pełna beta, ŻADNEJ poduszki stable
obie nogi crypto = pełna beta, zero poduszki stable
stable = poduszka (down med. −64% APR to głównie beta ETH połowy pozycji)

perQuestion.answer: A crypto/crypto pair like cbBTC/WETH carries full crypto beta because both legs are volatile assets, meaning the position falls with the entire crypto market and offers no stable-asset cushion. In contrast, a crypto/stable pair includes a stable leg that acts as a buffer against downside risk. The journal notes that for cbBTC/WETH, "obie nogi crypto = pełna beta, ŻADNEJ poduszki stable" (both legs crypto = full beta, NO stable cushion), resulting in a −51.5% HODL return and 61.5% max drawdown over 365 days. Conversely, the ETH/stable core is justified because the stable leg provides a "poduszka" (cushion), limiting losses to the beta of only the crypto half of the position.

citations.quote: a mostly sideways-to-down year
The 365-day year had flattered range-bound strategies
0 of 21 configurations passed the gate
a passive wide range ≈ HODL + fees − a little IL
narrowing added variance without adding expectancy

perQuestion.answer: The 365-day window covered a "mostly sideways-to-down year," which "flattered range-bound strategies" and produced a frozen algorithm that passed the gate on one pool. The 720-day window included a "strong uptrend," exposing the flaw: in that longer history, "0 of 21 configurations passed the gate." Five independent analyses agreed that a passive wide range was essentially "HODL + fees − a little IL," and narrowing the range "added variance without adding expectancy" because the flat episodes were too short (median 7.7 days). Thus, the apparent 365-day profitability was an artifact of the specific market regime, not a robust edge.

citations.quote: Wąskie pasmo to short gamma: każde przejście postury REALIZUJE dywergencję
We FLAT wszystko wygrywa
up 0% wygranych, śr. −13.91

perQuestion.answer: In an uptrend the LP earns fewer fees than in a flat market because a narrow range is out of position as the price rises. The journal explains this as “short gamma”: “Wąskie pasmo to short gamma: każde przejście postury REALIZUJE dywergencję” (a narrow band is short gamma; every posture change realizes divergence). Consequently, in UP windows the LP posts losses while in FLAT windows it wins: “We FLAT wszystko wygrywa” but “W UP … W DOWN: 20-42%wygr, wszystkie średnie ujemne.” The 720d breakdown confirms it: “up 0% wygranych, śr. −13.91,” whereas “flat 72%, +0.53.” The fee itself is not the problem—the narrow LP actually earned more fee in flat periods—but in a trend the price leaves the range, so the LP stops collecting and realizes losses on rebalancing, whereas a flat market keeps the position in range and fee-earning.

perQuestion.answer: FLAT_NARROW is a specific liquidity-position action (a proposal kind), not a general range algorithm. It is emitted when the flat detector confirms the price is stable (|gap|<2% for ≥12h) and recommends narrowing the existing range (e.g., from ±40% to ±5%). It is a discrete proposal with a concrete suggestedRange, costUsd, and paybackDays, and it pairs with FLAT_WIDEN as the counter-action when the gap exceeds 5%.

perQuestion.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) fetches the latest pool state by calling factory.getPool, reading slot0 and liquidity, and constructing a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It uses a fail-open strategy: if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the stale pool object instead of throwing. It is invoked in useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution immediately before buildMintStep to ensure up-to-date price data for mint calculations.
